_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). MOSTLY FOLIAGE, and the most leaf-dominated tile in z1lower -- roughly two thirds of its area is canopy. This is the right edge of the scroll and it overlaps t002 heavily (t003 x = t002 x - 0.234), so the same great deciduous tree fills it: gnarled ochre trunk at x~0.41-0.56, limbs radiating out, and a solid blue-green wall of large outlined 夾葉 leaves from x 0.29 all the way to the right edge and from the top down to y~0.80. What t003 adds that t002 does not have is the FAR RIGHT COLUMN (x > 0.77): more canopy, a distinct small dark-ink needle-frond shrub at x 0.815-0.955 y 0.625-0.795, a red intaglio SEAL stamped over the leaves at x 0.845-0.945 y 0.585-0.725, a single ink character 聖 on the rock at x 0.955-0.985 y 0.845-0.875, and a pale hemp-fibre rock slope filling the bottom right corner. What t003 loses off its left edge is t002's robed figure and its river sliver -- there is NO figure and NO water anywhere in this tile. The traps are the same as in t002 and are all in the left third and along the bottom: the vertical stack of rounded ochre lumps at x 0.11-0.33 y 0.50-0.96 is BOULDERS, not a trunk; the pink-washed patches at the bottom are ROCK whose long 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes fan out like needles; the ochre loop-chains down the left edge are bare woody vines. Rule of thumb that holds across both tiles: a blue-green wash means leaf, a flat ochre or pink wash with parallel hair strokes means stone or wood -- and the only leaves without any wash are the dark-ink fronds, which give themselves away by being repeated, paired and stalked.

objects.name: crown of the great tree, upper left of centre
objects.note: clipped by the top edge; the ochre limb threading up through x~0.60 is wood

objects.name: crown of the great tree, upper right
objects.note: solid leaf wall to the right edge; a small pale gap of bare silk sits at x 0.79-0.90, y 0.0-0.04

objects.name: canopy band right of the trunk, middle
objects.note: continuous with the crown above; split so the mask can be kept off the trunk fork at x~0.45

objects.name: canopy filling the far right column
objects.note: content t002 does not contain -- this is the right edge of the painting. Dense leaves right up to the silk edge; the red seal is stamped over the bottom of this box

objects.name: leaf mass sloping down-left off the crown
objects.note: the canopy's left edge slopes down-left through here, so the upper-left corner of this box is bare silk and rock

objects.name: the great left bough, clipped by the left edge
objects.note: the same bough that reaches out over open silk in t002; here only its inner half survives the crop. If both tiles are used, animate this bough from t002 where the whole shape and its clean silhouette are present

objects.name: leaf mass left of the trunk, middle
objects.note: right edge stops where the trunk begins at x~0.44

objects.name: leaf mass right of the trunk, upper
objects.note: a major ochre limb runs out right through this box at y 0.47-0.56

objects.name: leaf mass right of the trunk, lower
objects.note: the lowest blue-green leaves on the right side; below y 0.80 it is all rock and root

objects.name: low leaf spray hanging under the trunk fork
objects.note: sits directly above the pink hemp-fibre rock face -- do not extend this box downward

objects.name: small dark-ink leaf cluster beside the trunk
objects.note: same cluster as dark-leaf-cluster-right in t002. Dark pinnate fronds with NO blue-green wash; reads as a dark blot at thumbnail size but the glyphs are repeated, paired and stalked, so it is foliage

objects.name: dark-ink needle-frond shrub under the seal
objects.note: content t002 does not contain. Sharp dark ink fronds of fine paired needles springing from the rock, drawn far darker and crisper than the blue-green canopy behind it, with no colour wash at all. The most distinctive small leaf mass in either tile and the one most likely to be dropped by a colour-based mask -- it must be caught on stroke pattern, not on green

objects.name: fine hanging leaf veil over the upper-left rock
objects.note: SEARCH REGION, NOT A TIGHT BOX. Small 介-shaped blue-green clusters on long fine drooping stalks, drawn over the ochre boulder ledges behind them -- roughly half the pixels here are rock. Mask per-pixel on the blue-green wash inside this box; using the box itself would animate the rock

objects.name: fine leaf veil on the pale silk left of the canopy
objects.note: sparse scattered clusters on near-empty silk. Same per-pixel caveat

objects.name: fine leaf veil over the grey rocks, lower left
objects.note: the small-cluster layer drawn straight over grey ink-wash boulders and threaded by the hanging vines. Highest rock contamination of any box in this file -- a hint, not a mask

objects.name: gnarled trunk of the great tree
objects.note: thick ochre column with a knot-hole at y~0.66 and vertical bark strokes, running from the fork down into the roots at the bottom edge. RIGID

objects.name: major limb sweeping left out of the fork
objects.note: the wood carrying canopy-bough-left; visible in the gaps between leaf sprays. Leaves hinge about it, it does not move

objects.name: major limb running right across the tile
objects.note: the same limb that leaves t002 at its right edge; here its full run is visible

objects.name: upper limb crossing the far right column
objects.note: content t002 does not contain; a pale ochre branch running out to the right edge under the canopy

objects.name: bare ochre vines hanging down the left
objects.note: chains of small ochre loops dropping in long vertical strands from the canopy to the rocks -- woody lianas, no leaves and no wash on them. Not part of the leaf veil they hang through, and not rock

objects.name: ochre boulder ledges, upper left corner
objects.note: wandering ribbon contours filled with flat ochre-brown, no wash and no leaf glyphs. The fine leaf veil hangs in front of them. NEVER animate

objects.name: vertical stack of rounded boulders, left of centre
objects.note: THE MAIN DECOY. At thumbnail size this column of stacked ochre lumps reads as a second tree trunk. Up close it is 礬頭-style rounded rock: contour outlines only, no bark strokes, no branching, no leaves on it

objects.name: dark ink-wash rocks, bottom left corner
objects.note: the right edge of the dark foreground rock mass that fills t002's bottom left. NEVER animate

objects.name: grey boulders along the bottom edge
objects.note: clipped by the bottom edge; continues into t007

objects.name: exposed roots over rock, bottom centre and right
objects.note: long parallel 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre strokes fanning downhill from the trunk base; root and stone are drawn with the same stroke and are not worth separating. Rigid either way

objects.name: pale hemp-fibre rock slope, bottom right corner
objects.note: content t002 does not contain. Nearly bare silk stroked with long hair-fine parallel lines -- the quietest rock passage in either tile and unmistakable once you look for the parallel strokes

objects.name: pink-washed rock face under the low canopy
objects.note: DECOY. Warm pink-orange wash with hemp-fibre strokes fanning out in a spray that mimics a clump of needles. Not one leaf glyph in it. A colour threshold looking for 'not grey' will grab this -- that is the family of surface a previous pass animated by mistake

objects.name: second pink-washed rock patch, lower right of centre
objects.note: same decoy as rock-pink-face, smaller, and it sits immediately under dark-leaf-cluster-centre-right -- adjacent objects with opposite labels, so check this pair by eye if the mask looks wrong

objects.name: red intaglio collector's seal stamped over the leaves
objects.note: a tall vermilion seal printed ON TOP of the canopy and the dark shrub. It is paint on the surface of the picture, not an object in the scene -- it must stay pinned to the silk and must never travel with the leaves underneath it, which is exactly what a naive foliage mask over this area would do

objects.name: single ink character on the rock, bottom right
objects.note: the character 聖 brushed on the bare rock; part of an inscription running off the right edge rather than a stamped seal impression. Filed as seal because it behaves the same way -- surface text, pinned, never animated
